name: Draped blush

lead: Draped blush is a makeup placement style in which blush is swept in a layered, blended way across the upper cheek and cheekbone toward the temple, rather than dotted on the apples of the cheeks. The intent is a lifted, flushed, defined look.

Blush in general is a cosmetic used to color the cheeks and emphasize bone structure, giving a flushed and defined appearance. Draped placement is one way of using that effect, with soft layering to avoid a hard edge.

paras: People apply cream or powder blush in a thin layer, blend it upward and outward, and sometimes layer a second tone for depth. Cream formulas suit a soft finish; powders are used to set.
Risks are minimal: possible skin irritation from a product, and an uneven or heavy look if over-applied. The look suits some face shapes and styles better than others.

chain: Blush is layered along the cheekbone toward the temple
angle.text: The technique places color where it reads as contour and health, creating the impression of higher cheekbones and a fresh look. It is applied with makeup and washes off.

lead: Draped blush describes laying blush across the cheekbone area and up toward the temples in soft layers instead of a single round spot. The goal is a lifted flush that follows the face's structure.

Blush, also called rouge, is a cosmetic that colors the cheeks and is brushed on to emphasize bone structure, giving a flushed, defined look. It comes as powder, cream, liquid or gel.[1] Cheek color has a long history, from fat and red ochre in ancient Egypt to safflower-based rouge in China.[1]
No studies of the draping technique itself have been found; this article describes it as a makeup style.

paras: Modern rouge is brushed onto the cheeks to emphasize the bone structure and give a flushed, defined look; powder versions are typically talc-based.[1]
